items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: our guide explained to us the meaning of the designs in the tombs of the Pharaohs that were buried near the Sphinx.

ctx.x: When we finished at "Monseigneur" we had a few days to wait before the ship that would bring us back to France sailed from Alexandria, so Burns, his wife Louise, Beezie and myself visited Cairo. We made a visit of the Sphinx and the Pyramids of Ghizeh. It was a dream that came true because I had studied about Egypt in school and it was a big part of the holy land that I had learned about in Sunday school. It was like living in another world which in reality was another world and days gone by when our guide…

We visited the most famous Mosques of Cairo and rode camels around the Sphinx and Pyramids. We visited the first Memphis in the world where I saw many small Sphinx and a huge statue of who was perhaps the better known of all the Pharaohs in the history of Egypt.

We left Egypt and arrived back in Marseille the 30th of March 1938. Passed through Paris on our way to the Hague where Willie had one month's contract in the Tabaris which was my second time to play in Holland. And every night there was [were] at least ten glasses of Bols around my music stand and I don't remember every buying that many at any time.
